groups.statement: The system shall reduce manual paperwork.
The system shall allow the master or operator to review what has been recorded.
The system shall allow the master or operator to correct recorded information before submission.
The system shall work with data coming from other onboard systems where possible.
The system shall replace paper recording with a compliant onboard electronic logbook.
Crew members usually discuss fishing events, catches, and reports in very practical terms.
A haul or a set may be described as being recorded.
Status descriptions may indicate that something is pending.
The system shall support official terms that are more specific than the crew's everyday wording.
The mapping between official labels and crew working terms shall be aligned with fisheries rules and administration-required terminology.
The crew shall create the record as the activity happens.
Quick data entry shall be important for daily operation.
The system shall provide confidence that the submission went through successfully.
The electronic record shall start from go-live.
The system shall not perform a full back-capture of every old paper logbook unless there is a specific compliance reason.
The exact data transfer approach shall be agreed with the administrations and the operational team.
A record must be completed when a fishing activity happens.
The timing of the record must be preserved for compliance.
The system must support repeated updates when the vessel is still at sea or operating through several events in a day.
The transhipment report shall capture the vessels involved in the transfer.
The transhipment report shall capture the date and time of the transhipment.
The transhipment report shall capture the species and quantities involved.
The transhipment report shall capture where the transhipment took place.
The transhipment report shall identify the catch origin.
The transhipment report shall include enough voyage or trip context to satisfy the administration’s checks.
Some transhipment report details should be mandatory.
If a required detail is unavailable at the time of submission, the process should block submission or clearly flag the issue for correction, depending on administration rules.
Certain transfers outside the normal workflow, such as transfers involving a receiving vessel or port outside the normal workflow, may require different validation rules.
The landing report shall include the landing vessel details.
The landing report shall include the landing date and time.
The landing report shall include the port or place of landing.
The landing report shall include the species and quantities being landed.
The landing report shall include the trip or catch identifiers needed to tie the report back to the logbook record.
If the landing is handled through a specific market or first buyer process, the landing report may require additional fields.
Each regulated reporting event shall be sent to the administration that has jurisdiction for the vessel and the activity at the time.
The jurisdiction for a regulated reporting event is usually based on the vessel's flag state and where the event happened.
Some regulated reporting events shall be sent to a different authority than usual when the vessel is operating in another administration’s waters or when the landing is in a different jurisdiction.
Some reports may need to be copied to more than one authority.
The system shall allow an owner to check a record before submission when the master requests it.
The system shall support pre-submission checking of a record when there is a correction.
The system shall allow most entries to be submitted directly from the vessel in day-to-day operations.
The system shall allow company workflow rules to require shore-side oversight of records.
The system shall avoid delays that prevent time-sensitive reporting from being submitted on time.
Access to regulated records shall be role-based.
The master, crew, owner, shore office, and possibly a compliance user shall each be able to see only what they need to do their job.
Users shall be able to view and amend only the records they are responsible for.
Sensitive information such as commercial or personal details shall be protected from general access.
The system shall provide an audit trail showing who changed what and when.
Permissions should follow a person's current operational role rather than remain fixed indefinitely.
A person covering another role may need temporary access for that period.
If a person leaves the vessel or the company, their access should be removed promptly.
Temporary permissions should expire automatically or be revoked when the cover ends.
Amending records outside a person's normal responsibility should be restricted and allowed only with a clear reason and traceable approval.
Records created or changed onboard while the vessel is offline shall queue locally while offline.
The system shall ensure that no offline-created or offline-changed records are lost.
The system shall flag records with conflicts or incomplete data for review.
The system shall not silently overwrite records that have conflicts or incomplete data.
The submission status shall be clear so the crew can know what has been submitted and what still needs attention.
The system shall automatically import fields that the source system can provide.
The system shall automatically import position data when available.
The system shall automatically import catch data or gear data where relevant.
The system shall warn the user when data is missing, duplicated, or clearly out of range.
The system shall either hold missing, duplicated, or clearly out-of-range data for correction or allow submission only with an explanation.
The system may need to support approved hardware or minimum device requirements.
The logbook system shall work reliably on the standard equipment used on fishing vessels.
The supported device environment shall cope with wet conditions.
The supported device environment shall cope with vibration.
The supported device environment shall cope with intermittent power or connectivity.
If official platform constraints exist, the system shall align with them.
Platform constraints may affect offline storage.
Platform constraints may affect screen size.
Platform constraints may affect how crew enter data at sea.
The system shall be usable by crew with wet hands or gloves.
The interface shall be simple enough to support quick entry.
The hardware shall be robust enough for marine use.
The system shall provide enough offline storage to keep a useful history of records for the whole trip.
The software must be reliable.
The software must be secure.
Updates to official-reporting software must not be arbitrary.
Device changes must not be arbitrary.
Deployment must be controlled.
Platform changes may require approval or verification.
The system shall assume periodic updates to regulatory reporting rules rather than a one-time setup.
The system shall make logbook rules configurable.
The logbook shall support immediate capture of entries for emergencies, gear loss, accidents, diversions, unexpected landings, and transhipments instead of waiting for the normal end-of-day routine.
Exceptional logbook cases shall trigger different reporting obligations.
The system shall clearly indicate that an entry is exceptional and guide the user to the required information.
The system shall support partial completion of a logbook entry so the crew can stop and return to it later.
The system shall require capture of where an exceptional event happened.
The system shall require capture of what was involved in an exceptional event.
The system shall require capture of any immediate action taken in response to an exceptional event.
If the crew is interrupted, the system shall automatically save the log entry as a draft.
The crew may resume a draft only while it is still clear that the record has not yet been submitted.
The system should impose a limit on how long a draft can remain incomplete.
The system shall make repeated entry as quick as possible by carrying forward the vessel, trip, and gear details so the crew only fill in what changes each time.
The system shall provide a simple flow for adding the next fishing event.
The system shall provide a clear way to review the day’s running log before submission.
The system shall stay usable offline for long trips.
The system shall keep entries in sequence for long trips.
The system shall prefill information that is already known from the vessel and trip context.
The system shall prefill port of departure.
The system shall prefill active trip details.
The system shall guide users through the required steps in a sensible order.
The system shall offer templates for common activity types.
The system shall require users to confirm information that can change.
The system shall require users to confirm species.
The system shall require users to confirm quantities.
The system shall require users to confirm gear.
The system shall require users to confirm location.
The system shall leave some fields blank by default when there is any risk that the system could guess wrong.
The system shall always carry over the master’s session when a new logbook record is started.
The system shall always carry over anything already known from earlier entries on that voyage when a new logbook record is started.
The system shall ask the crew to enter or confirm context when there is any chance that the context has changed.
A new fishing area is a condition that requires the crew to enter or confirm context.
A new operator on board is a condition that requires the crew to enter or confirm context.
The system shall ask the crew to enter or confirm context if it has been offline long enough that the stored context may be stale.
The system shall prompt the user to confirm context before the record is submitted when there is a mismatch between onboard systems and what the crew sees.
Compliance-sensitive or event-varying fields should be left blank unless the crew enters them.
Catch disposition should be left blank unless the crew enters it.
Transhipment specifics should be left blank unless the crew enters them.
The system shall make the landing report immediate when the landing occurs outside the normal planned landing workflow.
The system shall make the landing report same-visit and immediate when authorities require it because of the type of catch or the vessel’s status.
The system shall use the routine trip plan versus separate compliance event distinction as the cut-off for deciding whether the landing report must be submitted right away.
Any significant change that could affect compliance should trigger re-verification of the onboard reporting software.
Minor cosmetic updates probably do not require re-verification of the onboard reporting software.
The crew should have a straightforward support route to report the issue immediately.
The crew should stop relying on the affected function until it is fixed or confirmed safe to use.
After a rule change or bug fix, the system should be updated centrally and then rechecked.
The system should provide confirmation that the version is compliant again before the crew keep recording.
If an issue is serious enough to affect submitted reports, the crew should be told clearly whether they need to resubmit or correct any records already made.
The master shall be the primary user allowed to create regulated records.
The system shall carry over the vessel identity to a new logbook record.
The system shall carry over the current date and time to a new logbook record.
The system shall carry over the home port or planned landing port if those details are still valid.
The system should allow non-declaration details to carry forward when starting a landing report.
The vessel should carry forward when starting a landing report.
The voyage should carry forward when starting a landing report.
The date and time stamp may carry forward if it is pulled from the device.
Landing-specific details should remain blank until the crew confirms them.
Quantities should remain blank until the crew confirms them.
Species should remain blank until the crew confirms them.
The destination of the landed catch should remain blank until the crew confirms it.
If there is any uncertainty, the system should leave the field empty and let the crew fill it in.
The system shall keep the receiving vessel or buyer blank until confirmed for transhipment.
The system may carry forward the last known port or area if it is only helping navigation through the form.
The system shall not prefill any detail that could be interpreted as an asserted transhipment detail without explicit crew confirmation.
The system shall be usable with very few taps.
The system shall provide big touch targets.
The system shall provide clear contrast so it is workable with gloves and in poor light.
The system shall support quick selection lists.
The system shall allow users to save a draft and return later without losing work if conditions interrupt them.
If the crew is interrupted by poor weather, device failure, or a temporary outage, the pressure to complete the draft shall be paused.
The pause on completing the draft shall apply only while the same voyage context remains valid.
The system shall allow auto-advance for purely navigational steps when the current field is low-risk and the next field is clearly dependent on it.
The system shall stop and require explicit confirmation before moving on when the entry is declaration-like, unusual, or could change the meaning of the report.
Once access is regained, the crew shall resume the same draft rather than start over unless the underlying trip or activity has clearly moved on.
The system may allow a correction flag only when the missing item is genuinely unavailable at sea and the crew can prove it will be corrected through the proper follow-up process.
The system shall change the rule only for exceptions agreed with the fisheries administration.
The audit trail shall capture record creation.
The audit trail should show when a record was viewed or exported if that is relevant for accountability.
Routine read events may not need to be recorded unless the compliance team requires them.
Access to the audit history shall be restricted.
Detailed audit history shall be limited to authorised owners.
Detailed audit history shall be available to masters as appropriate.
Detailed audit history shall be available to enforcement or administration users as appropriate.
If an issue affects a specific function, the system shall require users to stop using only that function.
If an issue affects a specific function and an approved alternative way of recording is available, the system shall require users to continue recording using that approved alternative way.
The system shall log repeated failed submission attempts.
The system shall log repeated failed login attempts.
The system shall show a clear validation message stating what is missing and why it matters when a required transhipment detail is missing.

If the missing transhipment detail appears to be due to a genuine at-sea unavailability, the system shall allow the crew to mark that reason and keep the report in a pending or corrected state only if the rules allow it.

If the missing transhipment detail is due to an external source problem or a crew mistake, the crew shall either correct it immediately or, if the source is down, use the approved fallback and sync it later.
A change that affects validation logic shall be treated as a new reporting rule.
A change that affects submission timing shall be treated as a new reporting rule.
A change that affects which administration gets the report shall be treated as a new reporting rule.
Changes that are mostly wording may be handled as configurable format changes.
Changes to the presentation of the same underlying data may be handled as configurable format changes.
